strongest_angle: Analyzing the canonical 1978 crossover novel Sherlock Holmes vs. Dracula by Loren D. Estleman, examining how the Victorian detective confronts the vampire starting from the 1890 landing at Whitby harbour.

key_facts.fact: Loren D. Estleman published the novel Sherlock Holmes vs. Dracula, or the Adventure of the Sanguinary Count in 1978 through publisher Doubleday with ISBN 0-385-14051-7.
In August 1890, a schooner runs aground in Whitby harbour with a dead man leashed to the wheel, triggering strange nocturnal crimes investigated in crossover adaptations.
A 1981 BBC Radio 4 play adapted Loren D. Estleman's 1978 novel, bringing together Count Dracula and Sherlock Holmes taking Whitby as its launching point.

quotes.text: Mr. Sherlock Holmes? His voice was as deep and devoid of emotion as the bass note of an organ in a cathedral. The detective nodded. I am Count Dracula.
quotes.speaker: Count Dracula
